newsitem.title: USA: Clinton delays Cabinet picks, says teamwork needed.
newsitem.headline: Clinton delays Cabinet picks, says teamwork needed.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he had decided to take more time to pick the key members of his new Cabinet after the current secretaries of defence and state emphasised the need to build a good team.

Clinton, who had been expected to name replacements for Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry by now, said those top advisers and others had urged him to delay appointments in the interest of picking a team that would work well together.

"I want to make sure that the team works," Clinton said, responding to a reporter's question about the delay. He said his advisers had told him: "If you have to take a little more time to feel good about the composition of the team you've put together by all means do it because it is the team that will rise or fall and that will advance America's cause."

He said the Cabinet appointments would be made well in advance of the reconvening of Congress in January, however. "We will make timely appointments, they will be ready well in advance of the Congress beginning, and they'll have adequate opportunity for the Senate to review them," he told reporters before leaving on a vacation to Hawaii and trip to Asia.

He said he was working with Vice President Al Gore, outgoing White House Chief of Staff Leon Panetta and his newly appointed replacement Erskine Bowles to put together the top team for his second presidential term.

The New York Times reported on Friday that William Cohen, a retiring Republican senator from Maine, was the front-runner to be named defence secretary. It said the secretary of state's job remained unresolved with likely candidates including former Democratic Sen. George Mitchell and Richard Holbrooke, a former special envoy to the former Yugoslavia.
